* [Attend to a set of interrelated engagement-support factors when designing remote and hybrid instruction](design-remote-instruction-around-engagement-factors.md) - This strategy directs educators planning remote or hybrid instruction to consider a set of identified engagement-support factors rather than treating engagement as a single lever.

* [Attention Breaks](attention_breaks.md) - Practice attentive behavior during non-crucial times during the school day.

* [Audiobooks for Literacy Reinforcement](audiobooks_for_literacy_reinforcement.md) - Audiobooks reinforce literacy skills, comprehension, and reading enjoyment by giving learners access to texts in audio form, with or without accompanying print.

* [Chunk Directions](chunk_directions.md) - Breaking multi-step directions and instructions into short, sequential units so working memory is not overloaded and learners can sustain engagement through a task.

* [Classroom Checklists](classroom_checklists.md) - Classroom checklists are structured visual aids that break tasks, routines, and assignments into discrete, trackable steps for students, teachers, and parents.
* [Classroom Climate Routines](classroom-climate-routines.md) - Recurring, predictable practices that establish a safe, respectful, and productive classroom environment so instructional time is protected and students feel a sense of belonging.
* [Classroom Community Building](classroom-community-building.md) - Deliberate design of interpersonal structures, norms, and shared activities so learners feel connected to peers and instructor, increasing engagement, persistence, and participation.

* [Direct Instruction](direct-instruction.md) - A teacher-led, explicitly structured instructional strategy in which skills are modeled, practiced, and assessed in small steps with high learner response rates and immediate feedback.

#### I {: #letter-i }

* [I Do, We Do, You Do](i_do_we_do_you_do.md) - A gradual release of responsibility sequence in which the instructor models a task, learners attempt it with support, and then perform it independently.
* [I Notice I Wonder](i-notice-i-wonder.md) - An open-ended observation and discussion routine in which learners first state what they notice about an artifact, image, or problem, then pose questions about what they wonder — surfacing prior knowledge and curiosity before instruction.
* [I Used To Think Now I Think](i-used-to-think-now-i-think.md) - A reflection routine in which learners articulate their prior belief about a topic and then state how their thinking has changed, making conceptual change visible.

* [Icebreakers And Introductions](icebreakers-and-introductions.md) - Short structured activities at the start of a course or session that help learners and instructors learn names, surface commonalities, and establish social norms for interaction.

#### J {: #letter-j }

* [Jigsaw](jigsaw.md) - Learners first master a segment of material in an 'expert group,' then regroup into mixed teams where each member teaches their segment to peers, making every learner both teacher and learner.
* [Jigsaw Classroom](jigsaw-classroom.md) - A cooperative learning structure in which each member of a small group masters a unique piece of material and teaches it to teammates, making every learner both teacher and learner.
* [Jigsaw Cooperative Learning](jigsaw-cooperative-learning.md) - An interdependent group structure in which each member masters a unique piece of material and teaches it to peers, making every learner both student and teacher.
* [Jigsaw Method](jigsaw_method.md) - A cooperative learning structure in which each member of a small group masters a unique piece of content and teaches it to teammates, making every learner both expert and dependent on peers.
* [Jigsaw Reading](jigsaw-reading.md) - Learners each read a distinct segment of a text, then teach it to peers in expert groups before returning to home groups to assemble the full picture.
* [Join national innovation networks and build internal leadership academies to advance responsible district AI adoption](join-national-innovation-networks-ai-readiness.md) - The report describes how Orcutt Union School District joined Digital Promise's League of Innovative Schools and created an internal AI Leadership Academy of classroom teachers and Teachers on Special Assignment to ope...
* [Jointly investigate fairness in machine learning with core ML researchers when deploying adaptive collaborative learning support](cscl-ml-fairness-joint-investigation.md) - The editorial proposes that CSCL researchers should partner with core machine learning researchers to study fairness in trained models used for adaptive collaborative learning support.
* [Journal Reflections](journal_reflections.md) - Students think back on their experiences and outcomes to gain a greater understanding of themselves.
* [Journal Reflections for Self-Awareness](journal_reflections_for_self-awareness.md) - Students regularly write about their experiences, outcomes, and goals in a journal to build self-awareness, metacognition, and self-regulation.
* [Journaling](journaling.md) - Learners regularly write reflective or exploratory entries about their learning, thinking, or progress to consolidate understanding and support metacognition.
* [Journaling for Metacognitive Awareness](journaling_for_metacognitive_awareness.md) - Journaling involves writing or recording thoughts and feelings to develop metacognitive awareness and build self-regulation skills.
* [Journaling for Self-Reflection](journaling_for_self-reflection.md) - Structured journaling practices that prompt learners to reflect on their learning, monitor their own progress, and receive targeted instructor feedback.
* [Journals and Learning Logs](journals_and_learning_logs.md) - Learners regularly write reflective entries about their learning experiences, reasoning, and progress to consolidate understanding and develop self-regulation.
* [Journals should actively solicit replication studies, meta-analyses, and large-scale impact reports](journal-call-for-replications-and-impact-reports.md) - The editorial's core recommendation is that a journal explicitly welcome and publish replication studies, meta-analytic syntheses, and reports of large-scale, sustainable, systemic impact.
* [Journals should adopt criteria appropriate to theoretical submissions rather than empirical-only rubrics](adopt-criteria-for-theoretical-submissions.md) - The editorial recommends that journal editors, editorial boards, and reviewers shift their evaluation culture for non-empirical work.
* [Just In Time Learning](just-in-time-learning.md) - Delivering instruction at the moment learners need it to complete a task, rather than in advance of it.
* [Just In Time Teaching](just-in-time-teaching.md) - A strategy where learners complete pre-class web assignments whose responses the instructor reviews just before class, using them to tailor in-class activities to actual student difficulties.
* [Justify GenAI integration through a when-how-why framework: proven contexts, specific implementation methods, and pedagogical reasoning](when-how-why-genai-integration-framework.md) - The article proposes that responsible actors develop an argument for \"when, how, and why\" GenAI can be used for educational purposes.

* [Logic Puzzles](logic_puzzles.md) - Logic puzzles are structured rule-based challenges (e.g., Sudoku, knights-and-knaves, grid deduction problems) used to exercise deductive reasoning, spatial reasoning, and problem-solving persistence.

#### Q {: #letter-q }

* [Quality Homework Assignments](quality_homework_assignments.md) - Assigning homework that reinforces learning, encourages real-world application, and offers enriching experiences.
* [Question Answer Relationships](question-answer-relationships.md) - QAR teaches learners to classify questions by where their answers come from — in the text, across the text, or from prior knowledge — so they can select the right comprehension strategy for each.
* [Question Answering](question-answering.md) - Learners respond to questions posed by an instructor, system, or peers, requiring them to retrieve, explain, or apply content rather than passively receive it.
* [Question Formulation Technique (QFT)](question-formulation-technique-qft.md) - The Question Formulation Technique (QFT) is a structured method for generating and improving questions to develop critical thinking skills, increase self-efficacy, and encourage participation in civic life.
* [Question Generation](question-generation.md) - Learners formulate their own questions about material — before, during, or after instruction — to activate prior knowledge, direct attention, and deepen processing.
* [Question students about why a correct answer was chosen, rather than why an error was made](question-correct-answers-not-errors.md) - In self-instructional kit work, the teacher asks \"Why did you choose c for number two?\" of a CORRECT answer rather than an incorrect one.
* [Question-answer directions that let children answer as part of the administration](question-answer-directions-young-children.md) - An implementable administration technique for young groups: the examiner gives directions through simple questions whose answers children supply aloud, so the answers constitute the real directions.
* [Question-based eLearning Design](question-based_elearning_design.md) - An instructional approach that replaces expository presentation with questions learners must answer, driving active information-seeking and knowledge construction.
* [Questioning](questioning.md) - Questioning is a powerful tool and effective teachers regularly use it for a range of purposes.
* [Questioning Techniques](questioning-techniques.md) - Deliberate use of instructor- and learner-generated questions to activate prior knowledge, elicit thinking, and deepen processing.
* [Questioning Techniques to Address Errors](questioning_techniques_to_address_errors.md) - Strategic questioning is used to guide students to recognize their errors and correct their thinking, emphasizing conceptual understanding over rote memorization.
* [Questioning The Author](questioning-the-author.md) - An instructional approach in which students engage with a text through open, author-directed queries ("What is the author trying to say here?") to build understanding during reading rather than after it.
* [Quick Images](quick-images.md) - A brief flash of a visual quantity or arrangement (e.g., dot cards, ten-frames) that learners reconstruct and discuss, building subitizing, number sense, and structural reasoning.
* [Quick Look Cards](quick-look-cards.md) - Brief, at-a-glance reference cards that give learners just-in-time support during a task without interrupting performance.
* [Quick Reflection Prompts](quick_reflection_prompts.md) - Short, focused prompts at the end of a learning experience that prompt learners to articulate their ideas, consolidate understanding, and surface their thinking for the instructor.
* [Quick Writes](quick_writes.md) - Quick Writes are short, focused informational writing tasks completed in under ten minutes, aimed at helping students process, organize, and remember information and ideas.
* [Quiet Classroom/Pockets of Quiet](quiet-classroom-pockets-of-quiet.md) - Creating a quiet classroom by reducing background noise to support increased Attention towards learning.
* [Quiet Environment/Pockets of Quiet](quiet-environment-pockets-of-quiet.md) - Reducing background noise in classrooms supports increased learner attention.
* [Quiet Signals](quiet_signals.md) - Quiet signals are predetermined, typically non-verbal cues used to quickly regain student attention and reduce classroom noise without raising the teacher's voice.
* [Quiet Space](quiet_space.md) - Creating a designated quiet space in the classroom allows children to self-regulate and reduce sensory overload by limiting auditory, visual, and other sensory input.
* [Quiet Space for Self-Regulation](quiet_space_for_self-regulation.md) - Designating a quiet space in the learning environment where learners can take breaks to regroup and calm themselves.
* [Quiet Time](quiet_time.md) - Quiet time is a structured period of 10–15 minutes where students engage in calming activities like reading, writing, drawing, puzzles, or meditation to transition back into the classroom in a purposeful and relaxed manner.

* [Self Explanation Prompts](self-explanation-prompts.md) - Prompts that ask learners to explain to themselves why a step, statement, or solution is correct, integrating new material with prior knowledge.
* [Self Monitoring Checklists](self-monitoring-checklists.md) - Learners use structured checklists to track their own performance, progress, or comprehension against explicit criteria during learning tasks.
* [Self Monitoring In Writing](self-monitoring-in-writing.md) - Learners deliberately observe, evaluate, and adjust their own writing processes and products against explicit criteria during planning, drafting, and revising.

* [What’s My Emotion? Game](whats-my-emotion-game-charades.md) - One learner demonstrates an emotion through body language and facial expressions while the rest of the class guesses the emotion, building emotional literacy through enactment and feedback.
* [What’s My Number?](whats_my_number.md) - A guessing game where one person thinks of a number and provides clues, and others use logical reasoning and deduction to determine the number.

* [When applying empathic design, consider delivery mode (synchronous and asynchronous), four dimensions of learner engagement, and three features of learning context](empathic-design-engagement-and-context-considerations.md) - Respondent Xie extends empathic design with considerations for digital delivery.

* [When implementing PS-I, include contrasting cases or build the instruction phase on student solutions](include-contrasting-cases-or-build-instruction-on-student-solutions.md) - Based on its synthesis, the review supports implementing PS-I with one of two specific design features: contrasting cases, or instruction that builds on the solutions students produced during the problem-solving phase.

* [When planning for the school year during COVID-19, schools and districts should weigh public health factors alongside educational factors such as potential learning loss](reopening-planning-weigh-health-and-learning-loss.md) - This strategy captures the publication's framing of how districts should approach 2020-2021 school-year planning during pandemic building closures.
* [When reading an evaluation, check that the study compared a group that received the program to a group that did not](check-program-versus-comparison-group-design.md) - This strategy tells readers of effectiveness research to look for a comparison between outcomes of a group that received a program and outcomes of a group that did not, since \"research studies compare outcomes for a g...
* [When scripting collaborative tasks, decide on the learner-agency versus pre-defined-goals trade-off position deliberately](agency-scripting-tradeoff-decision.md) - The editorial shows that the choice between leaving open what learners map or produce and scripting toward explicit curriculum goals is a live design controversy (Wise and Schwarz's Provocation #2).
* [When shifting to online delivery, first determine how students will interact with content, instructor, and peers](determine-interaction-modes-when-designing-online-coursework.md) - A concrete design step for instructors moving instruction online: attend to students' experiences and decide in advance how students will interact with the content, with the instructor, and with other learners.
* [When test dimensionality is unclear, compare several candidate calibration models to empirically justify the chosen composite scoring model](compare-candidate-models-when-dimensionality-unclear.md) - This strategy addresses practical testing situations where no clear a priori theoretical belief about the latent structure exists.
* [When uncertain about a learner's level, begin with high direction and support and keep reassessing](start-high-support-when-in-doubt.md) - Because special-needs learners are easily misclassified, the paper advises a default stance of high support and direction until assessment clarifies the learner's actual quadrant.
* [When using public reflection, agree in advance with all parties on what information can and cannot be shared to preserve confidentiality](set-confidentiality-rules-before-public-reflection.md) - The article advises that public reflection (blogs, discussion boards) carries a serious confidentiality risk for community partners and students, who may regret comments made out of inexperience.
* [Where Are the People Like Me?](where_are_the_people_like_me.md) - Learners examine media examples to consider who is represented and who is not, then explore the impact of this lack of diversity and how it might affect those who are misrepresented or not represented.
* [Which One Doesn’t Belong?](which_one_doesnt_belong.md) - Learners compare a small set of cards representing quantities and identify — and justify — which one differs, building number sense through structured comparison.
* [White teachers eliminate race-related hostile approaches and redesign school cultural policies to support Black students' belonging](white-teachers-eliminate-hostile-approaches-redesign-policies.md) - The review's discussion recommends that White teachers in schools upholding Whiteness make academic adjustments by eliminating race-related hostile approaches and re-assessing school cultural policies.
* [White-box-then-black-box sequencing: transparent study of a method before opaque delegation](white-box-then-black-box-sequencing.md) - Adopting Buchberger's principle from computer-algebra education, the article prescribes that \"a method should be studied transparently before it is invoked opaquely, and yesterday's white box becomes tomorrow's truste...
* [Whole Class Self-Monitoring](whole_class_self-monitoring.md) - Whole class self-monitoring involves the entire class participating in self-monitoring techniques, adapted from individual self-monitoring methods.
* [Whole Task Practice](whole-task-practice.md) - Learners practice complete, authentic versions of the target task from the start, rather than isolated subskills practiced separately before being combined.
* [Whole-class facilitated play of the virtual environments with multi-purpose content](whole-class-facilitated-virtual-game-play.md) - During deployment, the teachers changed the intended individual or small-group play so that \"the whole class worked together as a large group\": one or two students played while the teacher led the rest of the class in...
* [Wide Reading](wide-reading.md) - Sustained, high-volume reading of self-selected, accessible texts to build fluency, vocabulary, background knowledge, and motivation.
* [Wise Feedback](wise-feedback.md) - Feedback that combines high standards with assured support, framed to signal that the giver believes the learner can improve.
* [Withdraw mentor support earlier than currently thought, and calibrate how closely mentors work with mentees](withdraw-mentor-support-earlier.md) - Based on the finding that unmentored teachers, especially reentry teachers, progressed furthest through Fuller's stages, the authors recommend studying how closely mentors should work with new teachers and when suppor...
* [Withitness](withitness.md) - The teacher's communicated awareness of everything happening in the classroom at all times, which prevents misbehavior and sustains engagement.
* [Word Building](word_building.md) - Word building is a literacy strategy in which learners manipulate letter tiles or squares to construct words, reinforcing phonemic awareness, letter-sound correspondence, spelling, and word recognition.
* [Word Detective (Word Identification In Context)](word-detective-word-identification-in-context.md) - Learners search for and identify target vocabulary words within varied authentic contexts such as song lyrics, sentences, and familiar texts.
* [Word Family Charts](word-family-charts.md) - A word study strategy that organizes words sharing a common rime or spelling pattern into visible chart groups, helping learners decode and spell by analogy.
* [Word Maps](word_maps.md) - A word map is a visual organizer that promotes vocabulary development by having learners elaborate a target word across multiple dimensions — definition, synonyms, antonyms, examples, and imagery.
* [Word Of The Week](word-of-the-week.md) - A routine in which one high-value word is introduced, deeply explored, and repeatedly revisited across a week to build durable vocabulary knowledge.
* [Word Prediction Software](word-prediction-software.md) - Software that suggests words as a learner types, reducing spelling and transcription demands so composing effort can go to ideas and structure.
* [Word Problem Creation](word_problem_creation.md) - Learners select math operations and create multistep word problems for peers to solve, integrating math and literacy skills.
* [Word Processing and Technology Tools](word_processing_and_technology_tools.md) - Use word processors and other digital writing tools to support drafting, revising, and producing written work.
* [Word Processing for Composition](word_processing_for_composition.md) - Using word processing software to support drafting, revising, and feedback in writing instruction.
* [Word Processing for Writing Skills](word_processing_for_writing_skills.md) - Using word processing software such as Google Docs allows learners to draft, share, review, and revise their writing, with built-in features supporting feedback, revision, and diverse learner needs.
* [Word Sort](word-sort.md) - Students categorize key terms into self-generated groups before formal definitions are provided, then revisit and revise their sorts after instruction.
* [Word Study](word-study.md) - An investigative approach to spelling and word knowledge instruction in which students examine, sort, and compare words to discover patterns and generalizations rather than memorize word lists.
* [Word Study Developmental Spelling](word-study-developmental-spelling.md) - Word study organizes spelling instruction around learners' developmental stages of orthographic knowledge, using word sorts and contrastive word sets rather than memorization of arbitrary lists.
* [Word Walls](word-walls.md) - A prominently displayed, growing collection of key content vocabulary that learners access, use, and reorganize throughout instruction to move words into long-term memory.
* [Word-net exercises linking lexical knowledge to grammatical awareness](word-net-grammar-via-lexis.md) - Word-net exercises have learners build networks of private psychological associations around antonym pairs such as plentiful and scarce, attaching central adjectives to generic superordinate nouns.
* [Word-set exercises for contextualising vocabulary via imagined possible worlds](word-set-possible-worlds-exercises.md) - Word-set exercises are open-ended puzzles in which learners infer the intended reader, topic and purpose of a letter from lists of presented words, imagining 'possible worlds' that contextualise the lexis and accessin...
* [Work through four data-sharing decisions: what data to share, how to organize it, what documentation to include, and where to share it](four-data-sharing-decisions-sequence.md) - The guide organizes data sharing as a sequence of four decisions education researchers should work through: which study data to share, how to organize the data, what documentation to include, and where to share the fi...
* [Work with a coach or peer group, start with one insight, and gather data when applying learning sciences research](start-small-with-coach-when-applying-learning-sciences.md) - The resource recommends a staged approach to applying learning sciences research in classrooms, warning that \"applying learning sciences research in practice can involve trial and error\".
* [Worked Example Fading](worked-example-fading.md) - A strategy that progressively transitions learners from studying fully worked examples to completing partial solutions to solving problems independently.
* [Worked Example Routine](worked_example_routine.md) - A structured instructional routine — Get ready, Read, Discuss, Explain, You Try — that converts worked examples from passive reading into active engagement with expert solution reasoning.
* [Worked Examples First](worked-examples-first.md) - Presenting fully worked solutions before asking learners to solve problems independently, so novices study expert performance instead of searching for it.
* [Worked Examples Types](worked_examples_types.md) - Worked example types range from fully worked modelling examples (expert narrates every step and why) through completion problems and case studies, forming a guidance continuum from maximum support toward independent problem solving.
* [Working Memory Support Strategies](working-memory-support-strategies.md) - A family of design moves that reduce, segment, or externalize the working-memory demands of instruction so limited capacity is spent on learning rather than on holding intermediate information.
* [Working Out Loud](working_out_loud.md) - Learners make their in-progress work, questions, and reasoning visible to a network or community, inviting feedback and building relationships around learning.
* [Workshop-Based Writing Instruction](workshop-based_writing_instruction.md) - A structured instructional format in which learners draft, receive peer and teacher feedback, revise, and publish writing within a predictable workshop routine.
* [Wraparound student supports: navigator, financial supports, and job placement assistance](ibest-navigator-and-support-services-strategy.md) - Beyond integrated instruction, I-BEST provides a bundle of non-instructional supports intended to keep students engaged.
* [Write Alouds](write_alouds.md) - Write-aloud lessons, also known as modeled writing, involve an experienced writer (typically the teacher) verbalizing their thought process while writing.
* [Write children's reading material from direct observation of what children of different ages spontaneously attend to](write-books-from-childrens-spontaneous-attention.md) - The reviewer sketches a method for creating children's books: live close to the children, record what they do and say, and \"put into the books the things to which children of the different ages give spontaneous attent...
* [Write custom leveled readers that preserve key content and vocabulary across reading levels rather than using commercially available leveled trade books.](custom-leveled-readers-preserve-content-vocabulary.md) - The design team found that commercial leveled texts \"were inadequate inasmuch as the lower level (i.e., easier) texts were not including key vocabulary and information,\" which they conjectured contributed to CXI inter...
* [Write SMARTIE action-plan goals that are specific, measurable, ambitious, realistic, time-bound, inclusive, and equitable](smartie-goals-for-alignment-action-plans.md) - In Chapter 5, teams prioritize three to five high-level goals from the Chapter 4 tailoring activity and build an action plan in which \"goals should be\" SMARTIE: Specific, Measurable, Ambitious, Realistic, Time-bound,...
* [Write with a Transition Handout](write_with_a_transition_handout.md) - Before learners write, provide a handout of transitions, model where they fit, and explain how they guide the reader.
* [Write Your Own Word Problem](write_your_own_word_problem.md) - For homework, assign learners the task of writing some of their own word problems containing some of the key words discussed in class.
* [Writing Across The Curriculum](writing-across-the-curriculum.md) - Writing Across The Curriculum (WAC) embeds writing tasks in all subject areas so students use writing to learn content, not just to demonstrate it.
* [Writing assignments that have students talk, write and read through the writing process](talk-write-read-writing-assignments.md) - The second recommendation is to re-evaluate writing assignments, reconsidering the one-hour in-class essay and \"developing instead assignments that encourage writers to talk, write, and read\" while collecting informat...
* [Writing Conferences](writing-conferences.md) - One-on-one, conversation-based meetings in which a teacher and student discuss the student's writing in progress, positioning the teacher as coach rather than evaluator.
* [Writing Down Goals](writing_down_goals.md) - Writing down goals makes them tangible, supports prioritization, and increases commitment through externalized, reviewable commitments.
* [Writing For Real Audiences](writing-for-real-audiences.md) - Having students write for genuine readers beyond the teacher, with authentic purposes, so rhetorical decisions become meaningful and feedback comes from real responses.
* [Writing Process Portfolios](writing-process-portfolios.md) - Students collect, revise, and reflect on writing drafts over time, making their compositional process visible and assessed rather than only the final product.
* [Writing To Learn](writing-to-learn.md) - Using writing tasks as a thinking tool — short, low-stakes writing that helps learners process, connect, and consolidate content rather than demonstrate polished composition skill.
* [Writing Workshop](writing_workshop.md) - A structured instructional format in which students write for sustained periods, receive explicit mini-lessons, and engage in peer conferencing and teacher conferences within a predictable workshop routine.
* [Written Feedback](written-feedback.md) - Providing learners with written comments on their work that indicate quality, gaps, and next steps.
* [WWYD Critical Incidents](wwyd_critical_incidents.md) - Learners analyze short, ambiguous conflict scenarios and answer "What would you do if you were person X/person Y?", forcing perspective-taking and reasoned resolution before discussion.

* [Youth Participatory Action Research (YPAR)](youth-participatory-action-research-ypar.md) - Youth Participatory Action Research (YPAR) is an approach where young people collaborate with adults to conduct research and implement actions to address issues in their communities.

#### Z {: #letter-z }

* [Zoom Family Hours](zoom_family_hours.md) - Hold evening office or family hours on Zoom for parents and family members to pop in and ask questions or otherwise engage with you about their children.
* [Zoom In](zoom-in.md) - A visual inquiry routine in which learners examine a small portion of an image before seeing the whole, building and revising hypotheses as new evidence is revealed.

* [\"Document Outline\" Tool](document-outline-tool.md) - Students use the \"Document outline\" tool in Google Docs to extract evidence supporting the main ideas they've found in a text.
* [\"Headings and Highlight\" Strategy](headings-and-highlight-strategy-variant.md) - A collaborative digital reading routine in which pairs highlight key ideas and distill sections into four-word headings, then compare and justify their choices with text evidence.
